configurations.//: START HERE for the browser host. The static server runs as the debuggee so that stopping the session stops it too — a background task would outlive the session and the next launch would hit EADDRINUSE — and `serverReadyAction` chains the Chrome config off the server's own ready line, which is what removes the race a compound would have between opening the page and the first listen.
configurations.name: Start Order Flow Browser Page (:3002)

configurations.//: The one host whose code under debug runs in the BROWSER rather than in Node, so this is a `chrome` launch and not an `attach`. Normally started for you by the config above; run it directly only when a server is already listening. Breakpoints in the page bundle work as they read; the three heads run in a WEB WORKER, which js-debug attaches to as a separate target, so their breakpoints appear under a second entry in the call-stack view. Framework sources under `packages/` are reachable in devtools through the bundle's source map but do not resolve to disk here — the map's relative paths climb above the served package root.
